# Reporting

followed by these six sections:
1. Confi

 lists resolves via `get_symbol_sources` from its listing context.* It fails when the **file name itself** contains a character the selector grammar uses as a separator.

### Scala: `$` in the file name

`Constellation-Labs__constellation`:

```
src/main/scala/org/constellation/ConstellationNode$.scala      (21,932 bytes, exists on disk)
```

`get_summaries` lists `org.constellation.ConstellationNode` under that path. Resolving it from that listing context fails. `$` is bifrost's companion-object decoration in Scala selectors, so `path#name` where the *path* contains `$` is ambiguous with a decorated name.

### C#: a dotted file name

`Alex-Rachel__TEngine`:

```
UnityProject/Packages/UniTask/Runtime/UnityAsyncExtensions.AsyncInstantiate.cs   (exists on disk)
```

`get_summaries` lists `Cysharp.Threading.Tasks.AsyncInstantiateOperationExtensions.AsyncInstantiateOperationAwaiter...` under that path, and resolving from that context fails. The file name carries an interior `.`, which is also the fq-name separator.

### Expected

`get_summaries` and `get_symbol_sources` must agree: anything the first lists under a path must resolve from that path. A file name is chosen by the repository, not by bifrost, so the selector grammar has to survive `$`, `.` and any other separator appearing inside a path segment -- by quoting, escaping, or by splitting the path from the name on a delimiter that cannot occur in a path segment.

Unity's `Foo.Bar.cs` convention and Scala's `Foo$.scala` are both common, so this is not a corner case.

### Related

- #3302 (companion pair printing the same selector for both halves, closed) is the same underlying tension between `$` as decoration and `$` as content.
- The same tier found `apache__brpc` reporting a different path from `get_symbol_sources` than `get_summaries` listed the symbol under (`BUTIL_HASH_NAMESPACE`), which may share this cause.

### Reproduce

## 1. Confirmed cause with structured evidence

**The selector grammar is not the defect.** Measured at the base commit with the base build: `src/main/scala/org/constellation/ConstellationNode$.scala#org.constellation.ConstellationNode$` **resolves**, and the C# failure reproduces unchanged in a file named `Plain.cs`. `split_definition_selector_with_resolver` (`crates/bifrost-analysis/src/searchtools/selectors.rs:1337`) splits on `#` alone, so `$` and `.` inside a path segment are never separators. The regression test `a_path_segment_carrying_a_separator_character_still_anchors_a_selector` **passes at the base commit** — that is the evidence.

What fails is the **symbol** each tool prints, and then how it resolves. Two confirmed causes:

**(a) Greedy `$` stripping on a rendered name (Scala).** `FqName::render` (`crates/bifrost-core/src/analyzer/fq_name.rs:397`) appends exactly **one** `$` per `SegmentKind::Companion` segment. `ScalaLanguageSupport::display_symbol_name` removed **every** trailing `$` per dot-separated piece with `trim_end_matches('$')`. `object ConstellationNode$` is legal Scala, so its Companion segment's own text ends in `$`; the rendering carries two and the strip ate the one the source wrote. Printed `org.constellation.ConstellationNode` — verified `not_found`, because the identifier index holds `ConstellationNode$`.

**(b) A "not taken" test where an "addresses me" test was needed.** `addressable_symbol_name` (`crates/bifrost-analysis/src/analyzer/common.rs:76`) kept the undecorated spelling unless another declaration owned it as its own `fq_name`. C#'s `Owner$Name` and ``Owner$Name`1`` both display arity-free as `Owner.Name`, neither owns it, so both printed it and it resolved ambiguously. Measured before-state on TEngine: **7 of 53 listed elements satisfied the contract**; 46 were ambiguous.

**(c) Exposed by fixing (a): the same `$` confusion on the resolution side.** `codeunit_lookup_aliases` derives aliases from rendered names; `symbol_path_variants`' Scala reading and `split_segments_on_dollar` both strip a trailing `$` from every segment. `def run$` therefore acquired `org.constellation.ConstellationNode.run` as an alias — the undecorated reading of its sibling `def run`. Once each printed its own spelling, `collect_fuzzy_matches` saw two full matches for either query and could only report ambiguity.

## 2. Changes and reasons

Base: `18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19` · Final: `1ef2dd714fdbe5d6474c86121ee44ccbeaad7077` (two commits on detached HEAD; base confirmed an ancestor).

- `analyzer/languages.rs` — new `LanguageSupport::undecorated_fq_name(&FqName) -> Option<FqName>`. Decoration is a segment *kind*, so it is removed by changing the kind, not by editing a rendering. Default `None` leaves every other language on today's string path.
- `analyzer/scala/mod.rs` — implements it via the existing `scala_normalize_fq_name` (Companion → Type), gated on the name actually having a Companion segment. `display_symbol_name` stays as the string reading for callers that *accept* a typed spelling.
- `analyzer/common.rs` — `display_symbol_for_target`, `display_parent_symbol_for_target`, `display_identifier_for_target` and `prefetch_display_symbols` now work from the structured `FqName`. The contest test gains a second clause: a candidate that would print the same spelling contests it, **but only if it carries different segment text**. A Scala companion pair has identical segment texts (one name, two decorations) and `distinct_definitions` deliberately groups it under one selector (#2451), so that pairing is preserved; C#'s arity pair carries the arity *in* the segment text and is correctly separated.
- `analyzer/symbol_lookup.rs` — `prefer_recorded_spelling_matches` adds a tier the matcher lacked: candidates whose `fq_segment_texts()` equal a reading of the query outrank ones reached through a derived alias. `fq_segment_texts()` is the only spelling that never passed through a renderer. It is a no-op unless so

separator: `src/main/scala/org/constellation/ConstellationNode$.scala#org.constellation.ConstellationNode$` resolves fine on the base build, and the C# failure reproduces with an ordinary file name like `Plain.cs`. What is broken is the symbol each tool prints. In Scala, `FqName::render` appends exactly one `$` for a companion segment, but the display normalizer stripped every trailing `$` from the rendering — and `object ConstellationNode$` is legal Scala whose own name ends in one, so the printed `org.constellation.ConstellationNode` named nothing. In C#, a nested type and its generic sibling are indexed `Owner$Name` and `` Owner$Name`1 `` and both displayed arity-free as `Owner.Name`, so one printed selector resolved ambiguously and addressed neither. The common root is that the printing rule asked whether another declaration *owned* the stripped spelling rather than whether the spelling *addresses this declaration*. The fix takes the undecorated name from the structured `FqName` by changing a segment's kind instead of editing its rendering, and lets a same-spelling sibling contest the selector only when it carries different segment text — which separates the C# arity pair while preserving the Scala companion-pair grouping from #2451. Printing honest Scala spellings then exposed a second defect: `def run` and `def run$` in the same object became indistinguishable to the resolver, because the lookup aliases strip trailing `$` from every segment. So the matcher gained a tier it lacked — a candidate whose recorded segment texts match the query exactly outranks one reached through a derived alias, the structured counterpart of the existing `prefer_exact_lookup_matches`. On the two named repositories the contract goes from 16/17 to 17/17 on constellation and from 7/53 to 53/53 on TEngine. The `apache/brpc` `BUTIL_HASH_NAMESPACE` note does not share this cause: what reproduces there is a one-line offset between the listed and reported declaration line, identical before and after, and it deserves its own issue.
